scenes.name: Mohenjo-daro · city context
scenes.summary: Named excavation areas provide a city framework. Three monuments retain published dimensions; district extents, separations and ground levels are schematic.
scenes.orientation: North is +Y in the diagram. District placement is approximate; this is not a registered excavation plan or a single phase.
scenes.phase: Architectural synthesis; components may belong to different building episodes.

features.name: Unmapped city ground
features.description: The plain is a blank context for named excavation areas.
features.footprint: Display only; no city boundary inferred
features.placement: Display only
assumptions: Blank ground does not assert absence of remains.

features.name: Western mound · SD and L areas
features.description: The western mound carries the bath and other large structures. Its display rectangle is 200 × 400 m.
features.placement: West of lower town; proportions schematic
assumptions: The rectangle is not a surveyed mound contour.
The model combines named monuments without selecting one building episode.

features.name: Great Bath · Basin and brick lining
features.description: The published internal basin is approximately 12 m north–south by 7 m east–west, with a maximum depth of 2.4 m.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
assumptions: Wall thickness 1.1 m is illustrative; plausible display range 0.7–1.6 m.
The floor is drawn level. Joints show material, not individually surveyed bricks.

features.name: Great Bath · Waterproof layer
features.description: The caption describes gypsum mortar and bitumen beside the fitted brick lining.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
assumptions: Dark 0.07 m strips exaggerate the bitumen layer for legibility.

features.name: Great Bath · Opposed stairs and ledges
features.description: Two stairways enter the basin from the north and south; ledges cross the basin near their feet.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: Rise follows the fixed 2.4 m basin depth
assumptions: Ten steps per flight, 2.5 m flight width and 0.3 m treads are display assumptions.
Ledge projection and height are illustrative.

features.name: Great Bath · Colonnade and rooms
features.description: The source describes a colonnade on three sides, rooms to the east and a well in one room.
features.footprint: Arrangement described; envelope and room sizes assumed
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: 3 m walls and 3.5 m columns assumed; adjustable
assumptions: Four rooms and twelve columns are explanatory choices, not excavated counts.
Optional roofs show one possible coverage; the basin remains open.
The well diameter is assumed. No supply pipe is drawn.

features.name: Pillared Hall · Hall envelope
features.description: The caption reports an approximately 27.5 m square hall.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
assumptions: Later partitions and slope are omitted to expose the pillar arrangement.

features.name: Pillared Hall · Twenty pillar positions
features.description: The source describes twenty square brick pillars in four rows; only two rows remain preserved.
features.footprint: Published row and pillar count; exact spacing assumed
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
assumptions: Pillar width 1.25 m and equal spacing are display assumptions.
The full array combines preservation with the source’s reconstruction.

features.name: So-called granary · brick platform
features.description: The published envelope is 50 m east–west by 27 m north–south, divided into 27 blocks by passages.
features.footprint: Published 50 × 27 m envelope; block count described
features.placement: Approximate position west of Great Bath
assumptions: Passage widths and equal block spacing are display assumptions.
The traditional granary label is retained as a name; storage function remains uncertain.

features.name: College building · courtyard
features.description: The caption gives a 10 m square courtyard east of the Great Bath.
features.footprint: Published courtyard 10 × 10 m; surrounding complex omitted
features.placement: Approximate location east of Great Bath
assumptions: Only a courtyard marker is built; no invented 78-room plan is supplied.
College is a traditional interpretation.

features.name: VS area
features.description: VS is east of the western mound.
features.footprint: District footprint unknown; diagram patch only
features.placement: Published relative sector; rectangle and separations assumed
assumptions: The tile identifies a district; its area is not archaeological coverage.

features.footprint: District footprint unknown; diagram patch only

assumptions: The tile identifies a district; its area is not archaeological coverage.

features.name: DK-G area

features.footprint: District footprint unknown; diagram patch only

scenes.name: Dholavira · city context
scenes.summary: The city envelope and named enclosures use published dimensions. Walls, districts, water structures and gates are simplified; locations remain approximate.
scenes.orientation: North is +Y for display. Enclosures are squared to the display axes; source systems have different observed bearings. No new north measurement is made.
scenes.phase: Architectural synthesis; components may belong to different building episodes.

features.name: Display ground
features.description: A neutral plane encloses the model.
features.placement: Display only
assumptions: The 13 m site gradient described by the report is not reconstructed.

features.name: City envelope
features.description: Repeated prose gives 771.10 m east–west and 616.87 m north–south between identified inner corners.
features.footprint: Published corner spans; full rectangle inferred
features.placement: Axis-aligned diagram; SE corner unconfirmed in cited report
assumptions: The source table prints 711.10 m; repeated prose gives 771.10 m.
South and east wall survival is incomplete; the full wall is a diagram.
Wall thickness 6 m and tower spacing in this model are illustrative.

features.name: Castle
features.description: The report gives an external rectangle of 151 × 118 m and an inner top of 114 × 92 m.
features.placement: Approximate SW-sector location
features.vertical: 6 m display walls above a 6 m platform; adjustable
assumptions: Symmetric wall thickness interpolates external and internal rectangles.
The platform is schematic; the excavation contains several stages.

features.name: Bailey
features.description: The published internal bailey span is 120 × 120 m.
features.placement: West of castle; spacing assumed
features.vertical: 3 m display platform and 4 m walls
assumptions: The rectangular enclosure simplifies the published plan.

features.name: Middle town
features.description: The table gives 340.5 × 290.45 m for middle town plus stadium and 340.5 × 242 m excluding the stadium.
features.placement: North of citadel; placement approximate
features.vertical: 2 m display terrace; 3 m walls assumed
assumptions: The model uses the 340.5 × 242 m residential envelope and places the ground separately.
Internal street strips summarize the reported axial organization, not surveyed street widths.

features.name: Ceremonial ground
features.description: The reported internal span is 283 × 47.5 m.
features.placement: Between castle and middle town; placement approximate
assumptions: The title describes a conventional archaeological feature name.
Spectator stands and event activities are not reconstructed.

features.name: Lower town
features.description: The table gives a 300 × 300 m built-up area; prose describes major crossing routes and subdivision.
features.placement: Eastern half; position approximate
assumptions: The crossing strips are a spatial summary; no exact house plan or street width is asserted.

features.name: Eastern reservoir · Sloping stone basin
features.description: The report gives a 73.40–73.50 m top length and 29.30 m top width. The ordinary bottom spans are about 70 m and 27.70–27.75 m.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: General depth 7.20–7.50 m; model uses 7.35 m
assumptions: The simple continuous slope interpolates published end dimensions.
Local irregular masonry and rock profiles are not surveyed here.

features.name: Eastern reservoir · Deep northern probe
features.description: The excavator reports a maximum cut of 10.60 m in a limited northern probe. The extent of an equally deep central zone remains open.
features.footprint: Probe extent unknown; display rectangle 12 × 11 m
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: 10.60 m maximum cut from top datum shown
assumptions: The 12 × 11 m outline is a display assumption, not an excavation boundary.
The deeper cut is not applied to the whole reservoir.

features.name: Eastern reservoir · Three stair flights
features.description: The report identifies three flights of steps as components of the reservoir.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: Illustrative 30 steps through the general basin depth
assumptions: Each 1.6 m flight and its 0.5 m tread are schematic.
These steps do not reconstruct a single precisely dated phase.

features.name: Castle west gateway · Passage and slab steps
features.description: The excavator gives a 9 m long, 2.2 m wide west passage, with a small room in the south wall and steps at the outer end.
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: Slope, slab steps and 3.2 m wall height assumed
assumptions: The northern wall was washed to passage floor level; the north wall here shows a possible superstructure.
The model is a cutaway spatial explanation of the description.

features.name: Castle west gateway · South side room
features.description: A small guard room is reported in the southern wall.
features.footprint: Room existence described; 2.2 × 2 m display size assumed
features.placement: Approximate location in the city diagram; not georeferenced
features.vertical: Floor at passage datum; superstructure assumed
assumptions: The chamber opens into the south side of the passage.
Its designation follows the excavator’s account.

features.name: Castle well
features.description: The report records an internal opening of 4.00 m east–west by 4.25 m north–south, distorted by lateral thrust.
features.placement: SW castle sector; exact centre assumed
assumptions: The report’s 13.60 m evacuated shaft is not drawn to full depth in this city overview.

features.name: Basin and embankments
features.description: Rao reports mean long-wall spans of 214.87 m, short-wall spans of 37.26 m, and an extant height of 3.30 m.
features.footprint: Published mean wall spans; rectangular approximation
features.placement: Centered; exact trapezoid omitted

assumptions: Spans describe wall lengths; the model uses them as the wall-line envelope.
1.60 m foundation width is reported; taper to 1.30 m is simplified.
Rao interprets a dock; Leshnik and Junghans propose an irrigation tank. Geometry alone does not choose function.
